source_passage: essendo irritata contro alla Plebe la Nobilità romana, per parerle che la Plebe avessi troppa autorità, mediante la creazione de’ Tribuni che la difendevano; ed essendo Roma, come avviene, venuta in penuria grande di vettovaglie, ed avendo il Senato mandato per grani in Sicilia; Coriolano, inimico alla fazione popolare, consigliò come egli era venuto il tempo da potere gastigare la Plebe, e torle quella autorità che ella si aveva in pregiudicio della Nobilità presa; tenendola affamata, e non gli distribuendo il frumento
historical_event: Coriolanus advises withholding Sicilian grain to break tribunician power; plebs nearly lynch him; tribunes summon him to trial (Machiavelli's retelling)
administrative_actions: Senate sends to Sicily for grain
political_actions: proposal to withhold grain distribution as political leverage
tribunician citation to trial
outcomes: tumultuous killing averted
conflict channeled into legal proceeding
claimed_mechanism: legal accusation channel vented popular anger that would otherwise have discharged through extraordinary violence

source_passage: come accadde ne’ tempi che Francesco Valori era come principe della città; il quale sendo giudicato ambizioso da molti, e uomo che volesse con la sua audacia e animosità transcendere il vivere civile; e non essendo nella republica via a potergli resistere se non con una setta contraria alla sua; ne nacque che, non avendo paura quello se non di modi straordinari, si cominciò a fare fautori che lo difendessono; dall’altra parte, quelli che lo oppugnavano non avendo via ordinaria a reprimerlo, pensarono alle vie straordinarie: intanto che si venne alle armi
historical_event: Fall of Francesco Valori, Florence 1498: absent ordinary channels, opposed sects armed and Valori and other citizens were killed
political_actions: faction formation
armed confrontation
outcomes: Valori killed with harm to many other noble citizens
claimed_mechanism: no ordinary channel to resist a powerful citizen → both sides resort to extraordinary modes → armed violence
provenance: note: Machiavelli writes as near-contemporary witness; event historically attested (1498)

source_passage: l’accidente seguito pur in Firenze sopra Piero Soderini, il quale al tutto seguì per non essere in quella republica alcuno modo di accuse contro alla ambizione de’ potenti cittadini. Perché lo accusare uno potente a otto giudici in una republica, non basta: bisogna che i giudici siano assai
historical_event: Fall of Piero Soderini (1512): lack of accusation procedures against powerful citizens led opponents to bring in the Spanish army
political_actions: recourse to foreign (Spanish) forces
outcomes: fall of the Soderini regime
claimed_mechanism: accusations before few judges are ineffective ('i pochi sempre fanno a modo de’ pochi'); absent credible accusation channels, opponents call in external force
provenance: note: Machiavelli was Soderini's chancellor; this is professional-experience evidence

source_passage: sendo stato in Chiusi, città in quelli tempi nobilissima in Toscana, da uno Lucumone violata una sorella di Arunte, e non potendo Arunte vendicarsi per la potenza del violatore, se n’andò a trovare i Franciosi, che allora regnavano in quello luogo che oggi si chiama Lombardia
historical_event: Arruns of Clusium, unable to obtain redress within the city, invites the Gauls (Machiavelli citing Livy V.33)
date_uncertainty: traditional chronology; aetiological legend for the Gallic invasion
political_actions: invitation of foreign armed force for private redress
outcomes: Gallic attack on Clusium (and subsequently Rome)
claimed_mechanism: no civic remedy for private injury → recourse to barbarian forces
provenance: underlying Livy passage is V.33, outside Books I-X pilot alignment but within corpus

source_passage: caritas primum annonae ex incultis per secessionem plebis agris, fames deinde, qualis clausis solet
historical_event: Grain scarcity then famine at Rome following the first secession of the plebs (fields untilled)
outcomes: famine comparable to a siege; slaves and plebs threatened with starvation
claimed_mechanism: supply shock caused by withdrawal of agricultural labor during the secession
provenance: manual extraction 2026-11-16 (extracted from Livy before comparison with Discorsi)

source_passage: ni consules providissent dimissis passim ad frumentum coemendum non in Etruriam modo dextris ab Ostia litoribus laevoque per Volscos mari usque ad Cumas, sed quaesitum in Siciliam quoque
historical_event: Consular emergency grain procurement missions along three routes (Etruria via Ostia; Volscian coast to Cumae; Sicily)
location: Rome; Etruria; Cumae; Volscian coast; Sicily
actors: consuls T. Geganius and P. Minucius
administrative_actions: dispatch of purchasing agents in all directions
purchase at Cumae (ships then seized by Aristodemus as Tarquin heir)
attempted purchase refused in Volscian and Pomptine territory
grain shipped down the Tiber from Etruria
outcomes: plebs sustained by Etruscan grain; Cumae consignment lost; agents endangered
claimed_mechanism: neighbors' hostility forced reliance on distant suppliers (adeo finitimorum odia longinquis coegerant indigere auxiliis)

source_passage: et Velitris auxere numerum colonorum Romani et Norbam in montis novam coloniam, quae arx in Pomptino esset, miserunt
historical_event: Reinforcement of Velitrae colony and foundation of Norba as a stronghold in the Pomptine region
outcomes: strategic barrier established while Volsci weakened by pestilence

source_passage: magna vis frumenti ex Sicilia advecta, agitatumque in senatu, quanti plebi daretur. multi venisse tempus premendae plebis putabant recuperandique iura, quae extorta secessione ac vi patribus essent
historical_event: Senate debates the price at which imported Sicilian grain should be sold to the plebs; many senators see leverage to roll back concessions
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology (consulship of M. Minucius and A. Sempronius)
political_actions: proposal to use price as leverage against plebeian rights
provenance: NOTE: Livy frames the decision as PRICE-setting (quanti daretur), not whether to distribute at all

source_passage: in primis Marcius Coriolanus, hostis tribuniciae potestatis, “si annonam” inquit “veterem volunt, ius pristinum reddant patribus
historical_event: Coriolanus's speech: old grain price only in exchange for restoration of patrician rights (abolition of tribunate)
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; speech is Livy's composition
political_actions: conditional bargain proposed: cheap grain for abolition of tribunician power
invocation of prior secession (Sacred Mount) as threat repertoire
claimed_mechanism: hunger as disciplinary instrument: 'hoc malo domitos ipsos potius cultores agrorum fore'

source_passage: haud tam facile dictu est, faciendumne fuerit, quam potuisse arbitror fieri, ut condicionibus laxandi annonam et tribuniciam potestatem et omnia invitis iura inposita patres demerent sibi
historical_event: Livy's authorial counterfactual: the senators could probably have traded a lower grain price for the removal of the tribunate; whether they should have is harder to say
claimed_mechanism: food-price concessions as purchasable political capital
provenance: this is Livy's own claim, not event narration

source_passage: in exeuntem e curia impetus factus esset, ni peropportune tribuni diem dixissent. ibi ira est suppressa: se iudicem quisque, se dominum vitae necisque inimici factum videbat
historical_event: Plebs nearly assault Coriolanus leaving the senate-house; tribunes appoint a trial day; anger subsides into judicial process; patricians deploy clients and collective supplication; Coriolanus condemned in absentia and goes into exile
political_actions: near-lynching averted by trial date
client networks deployed to deter attendance at meetings (dispositis clientibus absterrendo singulos a coitionibus conciliisque)
collective patrician supplication
condemnation in absentia
exile to the Volsci
outcomes: violence rechanneled into legal process; defendant exiled; later Volscian war threat
claimed_mechanism: the prospect of sitting in judgment transformed rage into procedure ('se iudicem quisque... factum videbat')

source_passage: multis saepe bellis, pestilentia postremo amissa iuventute fractos spiritus esse; arte agendum in exoleto iam vetustate odio
historical_event: Coriolanus and Attius Tullius assess Volscian war-readiness: manpower lost to wars and pestilence, spirits broken, old hatred faded — artifice needed to provoke fresh anger
political_actions: war planning conditioned on morale and demographic assessment
claimed_mechanism: mobilization requires fresh grievance when old hatred has decayed

source_passage: Essendo la città di Roma aggravata dalla fame, e non bastando le provisioni publiche a cessarla, prese animo uno Spurio Melio, essendo assai ricco, secondo quegli tempi, di fare provisione privatamente di frumento, e pascerne col suo grado la plebe. Per la quale cosa, egli ebbe tanto concorso di popolo in suo favore, che il Senato, pensando all’ inconveniente che di quella sua liberalità poteva nascere, per opprimerla avanti che la pigliasse più forze, gli creò uno Dittatore addosso, e fecelo morire
historical_event: Spurius Maelius privately provisions grain during famine, wins popular following; Senate creates a dictator and has him killed (Machiavelli's retelling)
political_actions: largesse to the plebs
preemptive repression via dictator
outcomes: Maelius killed; incipient tyranny suppressed
claimed_mechanism: pious-seeming private benefaction builds dangerous reputation; early correction by emergency magistracy saves the republic

source_passage: coepere a fame mala, seu adversus annus frugibus fuit, seu dulcedine contionum et urbis deserto agrorum cultu; nam utrumque traditur
historical_event: Famine at Rome, 440 BCE: Livy records two transmitted causes (bad harvest year OR fields deserted for the attractions of city politics) without deciding
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; Livy flags divergent traditions (utrumque traditur)
outcomes: famine
claimed_mechanism: two competing causal accounts preserved, unresolved

source_passage: perpulere plebem haud adversante senatu, ut L. Minucius praefectus annonae crearetur
historical_event: Creation of L. Minucius as praefectus annonae (grain-supply prefect), a new emergency magistracy
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; office corroborated by libri lintei per Livy IV.13
administrative_actions: institution of a dedicated supply magistracy

source_passage: profiteri cogendo frumentum et vendere, quod usui menstruo superesset, fraudandoque parte diurni cibi servitia, criminando inde et obiciendo irae populi frumentarios, acerba inquisitione aperiret magis quam levaret inopiam
historical_event: Minucius's scarcity administration: compulsory declaration of private grain stocks, forced sale of surplus above one month's need, reduction of slaves' daily rations, prosecution of grain dealers; harsh inquisition exposes rather than relieves the shortage; plebeians drown themselves in the Tiber
administrative_actions: forced sale of surplus over monthly use
political_actions: scapegoating of dealers before popular anger
outcomes: shortage revealed, not relieved; suicides of plebeians (capitibus obvolutis se in Tiberim praecipitaverunt)
claimed_mechanism: administrative audit revealed the true shortfall; despair followed
provenance: KEY operational record for Phase V: this is a described administrative dataset (stock census, quotas, rations)

source_passage: frumento namque ex Etruria privata pecunia per hospitum clientiumque ministeria coempto, quae, credo, ipsa res ad levandam publica cura annonam impedimento fuerat, largitiones frumenti facere instituit
historical_event: Maelius buys up Etruscan grain with private money through guest-friendship and client networks, then institutes grain largesses; Livy conjectures ('credo') that this private buying had itself impeded the public relief effort
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; historicity debated; 'credo' marks Livy's own conjecture
administrative_actions: private bulk purchase via personal networks
political_actions: cultivation of popular following; consulship expected; Livy says he aimed at kingship (de regno agitare)
outcomes: crowds follow him; political threat perceived
claimed_mechanism: private procurement competed with and crowded out public procurement (Livy's explicit conjecture)

source_passage: hic Minucius eandem publice curationem agens, quam Maelius privatim agendam susceperat, cum in utraque domo genus idem hominum versaretur, rem conpertam ad senatum defert: tela in domum Maelii conferri, eumque contiones domi habere ac non dubia regni consilia esse
historical_event: Minucius, running publicly the same operation Maelius ran privately, learns through the shared personnel of both operations and denounces to the Senate: weapons stockpiled in Maelius's house, assemblies held at home, plans for kingship, tribunes bribed, roles assigned
population_groups: shared workforce of both grain operations (genus idem hominum)
political_actions: alleged conspiracy: domestic assemblies, bribed tribunes, assigned commands
outcomes: Senate alarmed; emergency measures follow
claimed_mechanism: operational overlap of public and private grain administration created the information channel that exposed the conspiracy

source_passage: opus esse non forti solum viro, sed etiam libero exsolutoque legum vinclis. itaque se dictatorem L. Quinctium dicturum
historical_event: Consul Quinctius argues the consuls are constrained by the appeal laws (leges de provocatione); Cincinnatus, past eighty, named dictator; C. Servilius Ahala master of horse
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; Livy cites the libri lintei for the annona prefecture in the same chapter
administrative_actions: dictator nomination to bypass appeal protections
claimed_mechanism: ordinary magistracies legally insufficient for swift repression; emergency office required

source_passage: haec eum vociferantem adsecutus Ahala Servilius obtruncat
historical_event: Maelius summoned by the master of horse, resists arrest, appeals to the plebs, and is cut down by Servilius Ahala; dictator ratifies the killing
political_actions: appeal to the fides of the plebs
extra-judicial killing ratified by dictator ('macte virtute... esto liberata re publica')
outcomes: Maelius dead without trial

source_passage: Maelium iure caesum pronuntiavit, etiam si regni crimine insons fuerit, qui vocatus a magistro equitum ad dictatorem non venisset
historical_event: Dictator's public justification: Maelius lawfully slain even if innocent of aspiring to kingship, because he refused the summons; goods confiscated and sold by the quaestors; the 'two pounds of spelt' (bilibris farris) jibe at the price of liberty
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; speech is Livy's composition
administrative_actions: public sale of confiscated goods into the treasury (iubere itaque quaestores vendere ea bona atque in publicum redigere)
political_actions: legitimation speech with catalogue of precedents (Cassius, the decemvirs)
outcomes: killing legitimated; property liquidated
claimed_mechanism: cheap food purchases loyalty: Maelius 'bilibris farris sperasse libertatem se civium suorum emisse' (hoped he had bought the liberty of his fellow-citizens for two pounds of spelt)

source_passage: L. Minucius bove aurato et statua extra portam Trigeminam est donatus ne plebe quidem invita, quia frumentum Maelianum assibus in modios aestimatum plebi divisit
historical_event: Aftermath: Maelius's house razed (site named Aequimelium); Minucius honored with a gilded ox statue outside the Porta Trigemina; he distributes the confiscated Maelian grain to the plebs at one as per modius; Livy disputes the tradition that Minucius crossed to the plebs as an eleventh tribune; tribunes exploit resentment at the killing to force election of military tribunes instead of consuls
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; Livy explicitly argues against a variant tradition (refellit falsum imaginis titulum)
actors: Q. Caecilius, Q. Iunius, Sex. Titinius (tribunes)
institutions: consular tribunate (military tribunes with consular power)
resources: Maelian grain, priced at 1 as per modius
administrative_actions: subsidized public distribution of confiscated grain at a recorded price
political_actions: tribunician agitation over the killing
electoral shift to military tribunes with consular power (only three elected, no plebeians)
outcomes: popular resentment partially bought off; institutional experiment with consular tribunes
provenance: price datum: 1 as per modius — one of the few surviving quantitative values in the pilot corpus

source_passage: Aveva questa legge due capi principali. Per l’uno si disponeva che non si potesse possedere per alcuno cittadino più che tanti iugeri di terra; per l’altro, che i campi di che si privavano i nimici, si dividessono intra il popolo romano
historical_event: Machiavelli's synthetic account of 'the' agrarian law: a holding cap in iugera and division of conquered land; elite counter-tactics; dormancy until the Gracchi; escalation to Marius, Sulla, Caesar and the end of liberty
date_uncertainty: Machiavelli compresses ~450 years of separate episodes into one continuous 'law'; no single such statute existed in this form
administrative_actions: colony foundation as substitute for distribution
political_actions: elite temporizing: armies led out, tribune set against tribune, partial concessions, colonies
faction heads created (Marius/Sulla, Caesar/Pompey)
civil wars
outcomes: destruction of the Republic ('fu causa della distruzione della Republica'); Caesar 'primo tiranno in Roma'
claimed_mechanism: contention over property (roba) is irreconcilable, unlike honors; delayed reckoning doubled the adversaries' power
provenance: the Gracchan and civil-war material lies outside Livy I-X: addition from other sources (Plutarch, Sallust, Appian tradition, Florus/Livian periochae)

source_passage: Dove Tito Livio usa un termine notabile, dicendo che con difficultà si trovò in Roma chi desse il nome per ire in detta colonia: tanto era quella plebe più pronta a volere desiderare le cose in Roma, che a possederle in Anzio
historical_event: Machiavelli cites Livy's remark that few Romans enrolled for the Antium colony, reading it as preference for desiring goods at Rome over possessing them at Antium
outcomes: under-enrollment
claimed_mechanism: desire operates on proximate, visible goods (an early 'revealed preference' reading)

source_passage: tum primum lex agraria promulgata est, numquam deinde usaue ad hanc memoriam sine maximis motibus rerum agitata
historical_event: Spurius Cassius's land bill (486 BCE): Hernican land taken, Cassius proposes half to Latins, half to plebs, plus public land held by private possessors; first agrarian law; colleague Verginius opposes; plebs themselves suspect monarchy; Cassius condemned and executed after leaving office
date_uncertainty: traditional Varronian chronology; Livy reports two variant trial traditions and prefers one (propius fidem est)
actors: Caeso Fabius and L. Valerius (quaestors, in one tradition)
institutions: domestic jurisdiction of the paterfamilias (other tradition)
resources: ager publicus held by private possessors
administrative_actions: treaty with the Hernici with land cession
proposed allotment formula (half Latins, half plebs)
proposed cash refund of grain payments
political_actions: first promulgation of an agrarian law
consular counter-mobilization
popular rejection of largesse as 'payment for kingship' (mercedem regni)
trial and execution; house razed
outcomes: law defeated; proposer executed; agrarian issue permanently installed as source of upheaval (numquam deinde... sine maximis motibus)
claimed_mechanism: largesse perceived as purchasing kingship; suspicion of regnum defeats distribution

source_passage: iussi nomina dare, qui agrum accipere vellent. fecit statim, ut fit, fastidium copia, adeoque pauci nomina dedere, ut ad explendum numerum coloni Volsci adderentur
historical_event: Antium colony (467 BCE): Fabius's compromise sends a colony to captured Antium instead of distributing land at Rome; triumvirs appointed; so few Romans enroll that Volscian colonists fill the quota; the rest prefer demanding land at Rome
actors: triumvirs T. Quinctius, A. Verginius, P. Furius
administrative_actions: appointment of a three-man land commission
formal enrollment of volunteers by name
political_actions: agrarian agitation deflected by colony compromise (consilio neutri parti acerbo)
outcomes: under-enrollment by Roman plebs; demand persists for land at Rome itself
claimed_mechanism: abundance bred disdain (fecit statim, ut fit, fastidium copia)
provenance: NOTE: Livy's mechanism (fastidium from copia) differs from Machiavelli's distance-preference reading — see alignment aln:c-antium-explanation
